Cyclone Akvan intensifies over the Bay of Bengal as IMD forecasts November 20 landfall in Andhra Pradesh, with winds reaching 145 kmph.
Cyclone Akvan: Third Storm in Less Than a Month Threatens India; Satellite Images Show Massive Cloud Formation Over Bay of Bengal
Cyclone Akvan has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, with the IMD forecasting further strengthening before landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20. Satellite imagery from INSAT-3DS and INSAT-3DR has captured extensive cloud formations, while coastal states have been placed on alert.
India is preparing for another major cyclonic storm as Cyclone Akvan gathers strength over the Bay of Bengal and moves towards the eastern coastline. The developing system is the third cyclone in less than a month to threaten the country, following Cyclone Arnab and Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu earlier in November.
Satellite images captured by India's INSAT-3DS and INSAT-3DR satellites have revealed extensive cloud formations over the southeast and west-central Bay of Bengal, indicating significant atmospheric activity around the system.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Cyclone Akvan had intensified into a severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 18. It is expected to strengthen further into a very severe cyclonic storm before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast.
INSAT Satellite Images Capture Massive Cloud Formation
Satellite imagery has provided a clearer picture of the developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal.
The INSAT-3DS thermal infrared images captured on November 16 showed a large, dense cloud mass over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal. Imagery from INSAT-3DR also revealed extensive cloud bands associated with the developing cyclone.
The latest IMD bulletin includes another INSAT-3DR image captured during the early hours of November 18, showing the storm's cloud mass over the central Bay of Bengal.
These satellite observations are important for monitoring the cyclone's structure, movement and changing intensity.
The IMD's November 18 bulletin placed Cyclone Akvan over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal.

The cyclone is forecast to move north-northwestwards and intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the evening of November 19.
The IMD expects it to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20.
At landfall, maximum sustained wind speeds could reach 120–130 kmph, with gusts reaching 145 kmph.
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha Under Cyclone Alert
The IMD has issued an orange-level cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to experience heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places on November 19 and 20, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall of 21 cm or more.
South coastal Odisha is also expected to receive heavy rainfall on November 18, followed by heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places between November 19 and 21.
The IMD has warned that strong winds could damage vulnerable houses, power and communication infrastructure, trees and standing crops.
A storm surge of approximately 0.4–1.2 metres above the astronomical tide is also likely to inundate low-lying coastal areas in parts of Andhra Pradesh during landfall. The districts identified include Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema, Kakinada and Visakhapatnam.
The impact of Cyclone Akvan could extend beyond the immediate coastal regions.
According to the IMD bulletin, heavy rainfall at isolated places is likely in Chhattisgarh on November 20 and 21. East Madhya Pradesh could also receive heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 21.
Eastern Telangana, Jharkhand and parts of Vidarbha are among the other regions included in the rainfall forecast.
These developments will require attention from weather authorities and disaster management agencies, particularly in areas vulnerable to waterlogging and localised flooding.
Fishermen Advised to Stay Away From the Sea
The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into several parts of the Bay of Bengal during the cyclone's passage.
Fishing restrictions apply to the southwest and west-central Bay of Bengal, with the latter warning continuing until November 21.
Sea conditions along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts are expected to deteriorate significantly, with very high to phenomenal sea conditions forecast before landfall.
Authorities have also been advised to prepare for possible disruptions to road, rail and air transport, power supply and communication services.
With Cyclone Akvan expected to strengthen further before reaching the coast, the next 48 hours will be crucial for monitoring its intensity, movement and potential impact on eastern and central India.
